text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** Every source I found agrees on that, with a few caveats.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** The biggest difference. Rated LFP stations typically claim 3,000-4,000+ cycles, versus roughly 500-800 for NMC models. At one full cycle a day, that is about 8-11 years versus under 2 ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed. One test peaked at 259 °C versus 731 °C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP is not fireproof, and in one overcharge test it reached thermal runaway earlier ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Its failures are just milder, which matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Cost over time:** Prices per Wh are now similar or lower for LFP, with a median of $0.55 versus $0.95 for NMC in one database ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.
- **Availability:** Most current stations are LFP. In one database, 121 of 128 models use it.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells store more energy per pound. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, to about 10-16% in two databases ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Some LFP units are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare actual specs.
- **Light, rarely used units:** If weight matters most and you'll use it a few times a year, NMC can be fine.

**Things that don't depend on chemistry**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F. Check the manual ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). One site claims LFP charges better in the cold, but others say it varies by maker.
- **Cycle ratings:** Check the end point. "To 70%" is a weaker promise than "to 80%", and test conditions differ between brands.
- **Sizing:** Pick for fit (watts and watt-hours) first and chemistry second.

**Rule of thumb**
- **Daily or frequent use** (van, off-grid, cabin): LiFePO4.
- **Home backup or indoor use:** LiFePO4.
- **Occasional use where weight is the priority:** Either. Compare specific models.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

**An LFP example:** The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating to 80%, and a 5-year warranty. It's not expandable, and it weighs 24.2 kg (about 53 lb). It lists at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF according to the listing ([details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)). [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). That's an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission, and the listing's own price and code check dates are from Oct 24, 2026. Confirm the final price at checkout. I only had a buy link for this model, so I haven't recommended others.

If you tell me your use case and budget, I can narrow it down further.
